svg.title: An Easter gathering with room for everyone

text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/04/05 - Essay - 01
Eggs are arranged together for a seasonal activity.
Pexels · 20821490
An Easter gathering with room for everyone
There is more than one way to prepare an Easter gathering. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two
useful starting points.
One reason is that clear instructions help children join an activity safely. For instance, we mark the egg-hunt area and explain which
places are out of bounds. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what
is happening.
Another reason is that recognizing different practices makes the gathering welcoming. For example, we ask families which activities
suit them instead of assuming a shared belief. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and
that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Persuade a group to change how they prepare an Easter gathering. Support your recommendation with two different reasons and a
practical example of each. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible
outline: introduce the situation; discuss clear instructions help children join an activity safely with an example; discuss recognizing
different practices makes the gathering welcoming with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
